[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Note on the "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller labels most clauses "[STANDARD]" and says they were "reviewed and cleared by both sides". Nothing in our playbook or instructions shows the Buyer agreed to any of them. Almost every "[STANDARD]" item departs from our positions. I have reviewed every issue in full and recommend telling Seller counsel that the labels are not accepted and nothing is agreed.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000), cl 12.1.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000). The 20% figure is a fallback only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and none has been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** We have no authority to offer the fallback, and the Seller has opened at our floor.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k with tipping basket.** The Seller's figures are five times ours, and a deductible basket erodes recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Limitations should not default across categories.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is unauthorised, and the default rule silently extends general limits to Title, Tax, IP and fraud.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Title and capacity subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title is the core of a 100% share purchase, and "administrative simplicity" does not justify capping it at 20%.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature". In effect there is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out.** This is non-negotiable, and the "any nature" wording would purport to cover fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (to 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room or public-register deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; delete DL 1.1–1.2 and accept only the specific disclosures in sections 2–10.** Blanket disclosure would neutralise the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause. Any qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** It is a blanket, constructive-knowledge bar that would also defeat the specific indemnities for matters we already know about (Ironquay, DD-006).

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m), so consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are insufficient.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion". DL 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is in hand.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require payout and releases at Completion.** About AUD 3.2m of secured debt with change-of-control and discharge mechanics (cl 8.1/9.2) cannot be left to a promise after Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and silent on on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs as a specific funds-flow line or deduction, or otherwise Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; add an express line item and an indemnity for the bonuses and on-costs.** The bonuses are Company liabilities triggered by Completion, and leaving them out shifts the cost to us.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The cl 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and called "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering title/ownership of the Project Materials and related third-party claims, while preserving the SOW3 cure (cleared payment of all fees, then transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3). Also a confirmatory assignment or payment receipt.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; broaden the indemnity and keep the SOW3 cure.** The AUD 180,000 figure (DD-010) is not independently verified either way, and no receipt or assignment exists.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a continuing investigation, regular updates, and cooperation and access rights through Completion. Our working assumption is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation; add investigation and information covenants and a specific indemnity.** About 1,240 records went to an unintended recipient, the scope is unresolved, and the Seller's "not material" view is not evidenced.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 330,000 total) treated as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued, ordinary-course and related to the others (DD-008/DD-011). There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold open pending diligence.** DL 8 itself does not establish ordinary-course status, so we should neither accept the Seller's label nor assert a deduction yet.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations "to all Claims", and Tax/IP fall under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant regimes, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the cross-category defaults; add an express hierarchy clause.** The drafting collapses every category into the general cap.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes it is only the source relied on.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as ASIC searches, PPSR searches, share certificates, constitution and board approvals, and a no-encumbrance confirmation.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.** It is an internal Seller-supplied record, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as OPEN. They are not agreed, and we should not assume unlimited liability or any resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax/IP as open items for separate negotiation.** No agreement exists, and folding them into a 20%/18-month regime prejudges the outcome.

---

**Overall:** None of the Seller's positions can be accepted as drafted. Escalation is needed only if the deal team wants to use the cap or time-limit fallbacks, which require Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. A suggested cover note to Seller counsel: *"The Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation or that any limitation or disclosure framework has been agreed. Our mark-up follows."*
